title.en: Pendulum and hinge as a reduced-DOF constraint

summary: Reduce a hanging or hinged body to the degrees of freedom the joint actually leaves, and keep an ideal pendulum ODE distinct from an engine constraint.
objective: A bob or door swings about a declared axis or pivot; lengthening a simple pendulum increases its small-angle period as the square root of length.
applies_when: A body hangs or rotates about a support and should not fly off as a free rigid body.
The viewer is asked to compare period with length or to inspect a hinge axis.
intent_signals: hang a lamp from a chain
door that only rotates on its hinge
example_prompts: Build a simple pendulum whose period I can compare with 2 pi sqrt(L/g) at small amplitude.
Hinge a shutter so it rotates about one axis and cannot translate off the frame.
negative_signals: A dangling mesh parented to a point with no length constraint.
A pre-recorded swing clip presented as a measured period.
not_for: Spherical pendulums, 3D conical motion or chaotic double pendulums unless those DOF are declared.
Claims that an engine joint automatically matches the small-angle formula.

principles: A pendulum or hinge is a restriction of relative motion, not a texture of a pin. If the bob can translate freely, there is no pendulum.

The ideal simple-pendulum equation theta'' = -(g/L) sin(theta) is an analytic model. A physics-engine revolute or spherical joint is a numerical constraint. They agree only under stated idealisations.
Small-angle period T = 2 pi sqrt(L/g) is independent of mass and, to that approximation, of amplitude. Large amplitudes need the sin(theta) equation or a measured period, not the small-angle badge.
implementation: Analytic planar branch: own fixed pivot, finite L>0,g>0, angle in radians and angular velocity; integrate theta''=-(g/L) sin(theta). Use a declared small-angle threshold for the approximate period readout.

Engine branch: configure coincident world anchors, with the bob center a nonzero distance L from its local anchor. A revolute joint restricts rotation to the selected axis; a spherical joint allows multiple angular directions and is a separate branch.
Apply point-bob period checks only to the ideal analytic branch. An extended rigid body has rotational inertia about its pivot; a generic engine hinge does not certify the simple-pendulum period.
Pause preserves state. Reset restores pivot, length, axis, angle, angular velocity, clock and engine body/joint configuration where used.
observable_checks: The analytic bob stays distance L from the pivot. Engine world anchors remain coincident within solver tolerance and motion respects the chosen joint degrees of freedom.
For the small-angle analytic point-bob branch, doubling L multiplies the period by sqrt(2); changing mass alone has no effect.
Beyond the chosen small-angle regime, label the approximate readout and do not force the nonlinear trajectory to match it. Pause and reset preserve their declared state contracts.

creative_affordances: Chains, gimbals or oversized hinge pins can make the allowed DOF obvious.
A ghost of the small-angle sinusoid beside the true sin(theta) path is a free teaching overlay.
known_limits: OpenStax simple-pendulum period assumes a point bob, massless inextensible string and the small-angle replacement of sin(theta) by theta.
Rapier joints restrict relative DOF; they do not implement the pendulum closed form or guarantee energy conservation.
Authored reusable guidance; no runtime artifact has been observed for this record.

claims.statement: A simple pendulum of length L has angular acceleration -(g/L) sin(theta); for small angles the motion is simple harmonic with period 2 pi sqrt(L/g), independent of mass and, in that approximation, of amplitude.
claims.scope: Ideal planar point bob, fixed pivot, finite positive L and g and a massless inextensible taut support; approximate period is for small angles, not extended rigid bodies or spherical trajectories.

source_refs.locator: 15.4, The Simple Pendulum, theta''=-(g/L)sin(theta) and T=2 pi sqrt(L/g)

claims.statement: A Rapier revolute joint prevents any relative movement between two rigid bodies except relative rotation along one axis; a spherical joint keeps two local anchors coincident and is documented as typical for pendulums and ragdoll arms.
claims.scope: Rapier JavaScript joint types; not an analytic period formula.
